autoLink.name: Auto-Link Entry Names
autoLink.hint: Newly-typed mentions of other Enhanced Journal entry names — in page text, session recaps and GM notes — become links when the page is saved. Linking stays within the entry's campaign (plus unfiled entries). Existing links, code blocks, and pages flagged to opt out are left untouched.

autoCaptureEncounters.name: Auto-Capture Encounters
autoCaptureEncounters.hint: When enabled, starting a combat creates an Encounter journal entry from its participants, and ending it adds the outcome. The entry is filed onto the campaign timeline's newest timepoint.

autoCaptureSharedMedia.name: Auto-Capture Shared Media
autoCaptureSharedMedia.hint: When enabled, images and videos a GM shows to players are automatically filed onto the campaign timeline's newest timepoint.

playersWriteSessions.name: Players Write Sessions (outside campaigns)
playersWriteSessions.hint: Sessions created inside a campaign whose Player access is at least "Players can view" are already editable by players (re-apply the baseline to cover older ones). Turn this on only to make sessions outside any campaign player-editable too; it also offers ownership of existing sessions.
playersWriteSessions.applyExisting: Grant all players ownership of {count} existing session entries? Sessions created from now on are already covered.
playersWriteSessions.applyFailed: Granting session ownership failed — see the console.

shellHosting.name: Host the Campaign Hub and Sessions inside Monk's Enhanced Journal
shellHosting.hint: Native mode only. Off: the Hub and Session sheets open as standalone windows.

retroLinkMode.name: Retroactive Auto-Link
retroLinkMode.hint: When a new Enhanced Journal entry is created, link existing plain-text mentions of its name in its campaign (and unfiled entries), including session recaps and GM notes. Silent writes immediately and shows a notification; Confirm shows the GM a review dialog first.

warnPlayerAccess.name: Warn when Campaign Companion can't work for players
warnPlayerAccess.hint: When a GM logs in and Monk's Enhanced Journal's "Allow players to use Enhanced Journal" setting is off, explain that Campaign Companion won't work properly for players and offer to turn it on.

autoStartSession.name: Offer to start a session at login
autoStartSession.hint: When a GM logs in and no session is open in a campaign that hasn't had one today, ask whether to start one.

playerConnectionsEnabled.name: Players can add party relationships
playerConnectionsEnabled.hint: Campaign Contributors can add, label and remove the party's relationships between entries. Off: existing party relationships still show, read-only for players.

lines.sessions: Each game night is a Session. Your GM starts one; it lists who was there, the shared recap, and when it happened in the world.
lines.notes: Write what happened in the Session's recap. Mention a person or place by name and it becomes a link when you save.
lines.entries: Entries are the people, places, quests and things your GM has written up. Search finds words inside them; Entries lists them all.
lines.reveals: When your GM reveals a secret to you, you get a whisper in chat and the text appears on the entry with an orange rule.
lines.lookBack: Sessions and Timeline show what happened in order. Graph shows how entries connect; click a node to focus on it.

playerAccess.title: Campaign Companion: players need Enhanced Journal access
playerAccess.body1: Campaign Companion won't work properly for your players while Monk's Enhanced Journal's "Allow players to use Enhanced Journal" setting is off.
playerAccess.body2: With it off, players can't use the Campaign Hub, Session sheets, the knowledge panel or campaign entries the way the companion expects. Anything they open or create opens in Foundry's default journal editor instead.
playerAccess.body3: Turn it on now to make Campaign Companion work for players?

playerAccess.reloadBody: Your GM has enabled Campaign Companion for players. Reload now to use it?
